title: Bell Sleeve Top Sewing Pattern – Free PDF
content:
Garment Fitted boat neck top with bell sleeves

Level Intermediate

Sizes US 00 – 22 (XXS – 4XL)

Fabric Viscose crepe, crepe de chine, viscose challis or light linen-viscose

Pieces 5

This free bell sleeve top sewing pattern gives you a fitted, hip-length top with a wide boat neckline and long sleeves that flare from the elbow into a soft bell. The neckline is finished with a clean facing and an invisible zipper in the left side seam lets you slip it on, so the front stays smooth with no darts at all.

→ Jump to the free download

1 cm (3/8″) seam allowance included on all pieces · 2 cm (3/4″) hem on the body and sleeves · invisible zipper 50 cm (20″) in the left side seam

Design details of the bell sleeve top

Think of a seventies blouse made modern: the body is cut close from the bust to the hips, with about 3 cm of ease at the bust and hip, and the only seam you see is the centre back seam. All the drama goes into the sleeves, which stay slim on the upper arm and open into a wide bell from the elbow down to just past the wrist.

Reading the sketch

On the front, the neckline runs almost straight across from shoulder to shoulder: that is the boat neck. The lines inside the sleeves are only folds of the bell, not seams. There are no darts, no princess lines and no pockets on the body.

On the back you can see the centre back seam running down the middle and a back neckline that dips a little lower than the front. The invisible zipper sits in the left side seam, so it does not show on either view.

  • Wide, shallow boat neckline finished with an interfaced facing, no topstitching
  • Long set-in sleeves, slim on the upper arm and flaring into a bell from the elbow
  • Close fit with a centre back seam and no darts
  • Invisible zipper in the left side seam, opening from the hem
  • Hip length with a gently curved hem, 2 cm (3/4″) hem on the body and sleeves

This is a lovely next step after your first easy tops: only five pieces, but you will practise three classic techniques, a set-in sleeve, a neck facing and an invisible zipper, on a top you will actually want to wear.

Sizing guide

Measure your bust around the fullest part and pick the size from the table, then check your waist and hips. This top is close fitting, so between two sizes take the larger one. Not sure how to measure? See how to take body measurements and how to choose your pattern size.

US sizes 00 to 22, drafted for a height of 167.75 cm (5 ft 6 in). Letter sizes are a guide only: 00 = XXS · 0–2 = XS · 4–6 = S · 8–10 = M · 12–14 = L · 16 = XL · 18 = 2XL · 20 = 3XL · 22 = 4XL. Always choose by measurements.

Body measurements

Finished top measurements

There is about 3 cm (1 1/4″) of ease at the bust and hip and 4 cm (1 1/2″) at the waist. Back length is measured at the centre back from the neckline seam to the finished hem; sleeve opening is the full width around the sleeve hem.

Fabric amounts

Estimated with every piece laid out for each size, plus about 8 % for shrinkage and straightening. Buy a little more for a one-way print, and pre-wash the fabric before cutting.

Common fit adjustments

Length. The top is drafted for 167.75 cm. Add or remove length evenly at the hem of the front and back, keep the curve, and move the lower zipper notch with the hemline. Full guide: how to lengthen or shorten a sewing pattern.

Sleeve length. Bell sleeves look best ending just past the wrist. Lengthen or shorten the sleeve above the elbow, where it is still straight, so the flare keeps its shape.

Materials

  • Main fabric: 1.5 to 2.8 m (1 3/4 to 3 1/8 yd) of a light to medium-weight woven with drape
  • Interfacing: 0.2 m (1/4 yd) of light fusible interfacing for the neck facings
  • Zipper: one invisible zipper, 50 cm (20″); a 45 cm (18″) zipper also works
  • Thread: polyester all-purpose thread
  • Tools: invisible zipper foot, universal or microtex needle 70 to 80
  • Pins or clips, chalk or a washable marker

Pattern pieces

  • 1 Front: cut 1 on a single layer, right side up (drawn whole)
  • 2 Back: cut 2, a left and a right piece
  • 3 Sleeve: cut 2, a left and a right piece
  • 4 Front neck facing: cut 1 + 1 in interfacing (drawn whole)
  • 5 Back neck facing: cut 2 + 2 in interfacing

Choosing fabric for a bell sleeve top

The sleeves decide the fabric. They need drape so the bell falls in soft folds instead of standing away from the arm, so look for a light to medium-weight woven that moves: viscose or polyester crepe, crepe de chine, viscose challis or a light linen-viscose blend. Crepe is the easiest to sew and gives that smooth, matte look; challis is softer and cooler for warmer days.

Because the body is close fitting, a woven with 2 to 5 % elastane makes the top more comfortable to move in. Avoid stiff cottons and denim (the bells will stick out) and very sheer fabrics, where the neck facing would show through. More tips in how to choose fabric for sewing patterns and how to use fusible interfacing.

Sewing notes

Fit and style

A close fit from bust to hip with dramatic sleeves. Make a quick test of the body in a cheap fabric if you are between sizes.

Fabric

Drapey wovens only: the bells need movement. Use a pressing cloth on crepe to avoid shine.

Zipper

The invisible zipper is set upside down, opening from the hem. See how to sew a zipper.

Get the pattern

Free PDF pattern, one file per size, US sizes 00 to 22 (XXS to 4XL). Share your make with #sewcraftly!

Download A4
Download US Letter

Print page 1 at 100% and check that the test square measures 10 cm (4 in). New to PDF patterns? Read how to print and assemble a PDF pattern.

Sewing steps

Seam allowance 1 cm (3/8″) unless stated otherwise. Sew right sides together and press every seam before it is crossed by another one.

  1. Prepare. Fuse light interfacing to the front neck facing and both back neck facings. Staystitch the neckline of the front and both backs 8 mm from the edge so the wide boat neckline does not stretch, and finish the side, shoulder and centre back edges separately.
  2. Centre back seam. Pin the two backs right sides together, matching the notch, and stitch from the neckline to the hem. Press the seam open.
  3. Shoulders. Pin the front to the back at the shoulders, stitch and press the seams open.
  4. Neck facing. Join the back facings at the centre back, then the front facing to them at the shoulders. Finish the outer edge, pin the facing to the neckline right sides together, matching the centre front, the notches, the shoulder seams and the centre back, and stitch. Trim, clip the curves, understitch, turn the facing inside and tack it at the shoulders.
  5. Side seams. Sew the right side seam from the underarm to the hem. On the left side, stitch only from the underarm down to the upper zipper notch and backstitch firmly.
  6. Invisible zipper. Baste the rest of the left side seam and press it open. Place the zipper upside down, pull end at the hem, with its top stop at the lower zipper notch, just above the hemline. Undo the basting and stitch each tape close to the teeth with an invisible zipper foot, from the hem up to the upper notch. Bar-tack across the coil above the notch and cut the excess.
  7. Sleeves. Easestitch the sleeve cap between the two circles, sew the underarm seam and hem the flared edge with a narrow double hem (1 cm + 1 cm). Set each sleeve into its armhole, single notch to the front, double notches to the back, top notch to the shoulder, then stitch, finish and press toward the sleeve.
  8. Hem. Finish the lower edge, fold the zipper tape ends away into the hem allowance and turn up 2 cm (3/4″). Stitch by machine or with a blind hem, slipstitch the hem ends to the zipper tape and give the top a final press.

Tips and common mistakes

A neckline that gapes or stretches. The boat neck is cut on a long curve that stretches easily. Staystitch it as soon as the pieces are cut, handle it flat, and understitch the facing so it rolls neatly to the inside.

Puckers on the sleeve cap. Spread the ease evenly between the two circles before you pin, and sew with the sleeve on top so you can see and smooth any small folds.

A wavy zipper. Do not stretch the side seam while you sew, and press the zipper coil flat with a cool iron before you start so the stitches can sit close to the teeth.

Bells that twist. Cut the sleeves exactly on the grain and hem them with a narrow double hem, easing the fullness along the curve instead of pulling it flat.

How to style a bell sleeve top

Seventies look: tuck it into high-waisted flares in a matching tone, with platform boots or clogs.

Easy everyday: wear it loose over wide-leg trousers in linen or cotton. It pairs beautifully with our free wide leg pants sewing pattern.

Evening: a black or deep red crepe with slim trousers and small gold jewellery. For a bolder outfit, try it with our free flare pants sewing pattern.

Care

Wash at 30 °C (cold) on a gentle cycle, inside out, with the zipper closed. Dry flat or on a hanger and press with a pressing cloth; a little steam brings back the drape of the sleeves.

Questions

Is seam allowance included?

Yes: 1 cm (3/8″) on every edge, plus a 2 cm (3/4″) hem on the body and on the sleeves.

Which paper sizes are included?

The free download has A4 and US Letter files, one file per size, so you only print the size you need.

Which size should I choose?

Choose by your bust measurement in the size chart, not by your shop size. The top is close fitting: between two sizes, or with a fabric that has no stretch at all, take the larger one.

How do I get the top on?

An invisible zipper in the left side seam opens from the hem up to just below the underarm, so the fitted top slips on easily without a back opening.

Is this bell sleeve top hard to sew?

It is a good intermediate project. There are only five pieces and no darts, but you will set in sleeves, finish the boat neckline with a facing and insert an invisible zipper.

What fabric works best?

A light to medium-weight woven with drape: viscose crepe, polyester crepe, crepe de chine, viscose challis or a light linen-viscose. A little elastane (2 to 5 %) makes the close fit more comfortable.

Can I make the sleeves less dramatic?

Yes. Trace the sleeve and take some width off both side seams of the sleeve below the elbow, keeping the same length. Do the same amount on both edges so the bell stays balanced.

Can I make it longer or shorter?

Yes. The pattern is drafted for a height of 167.75 cm (5 ft 6 in). Add or remove length evenly at the hem of the front and back, keep the curve, and move the lower zipper notch with the hemline.
